title: Any settings.tools.core value (even []) emits a wildcard DENY that silently excludes all MCP tools – breaks run-gemini-cli's shipped pr-review example

triage_metadata.reasoning: The issue is a detailed and actionable bug report identifying a specific defect in policy enforcement where setting tools.core creates a wildcard DENY rule that unintentionally blocks MCP tools, complete with reproduction steps, root cause analysis, and affected source locations.
triage_metadata.effort_reasoning: The required change is a localized fix within packages/core/src/policy/config.ts to adjust the core tool default DENY rule so that it does not override MCP tool permissions, alongside adding unit tests in packages/core/src/policy/config.test.ts.

summary.problem: Setting tools.core in settings (including tools.core: []) creates a wildcard DENY policy rule that outranks MCP tool allow rules, silently excluding all MCP tools from the registry.
summary.root_cause: In packages/core/src/policy/config.ts, when settings.tools.core is present, a wildcard DENY rule (toolName: '*') is added at priority CORE_TOOLS_FLAG_PRIORITY - 0.01 (4.24). This priority outranks TRUSTED_MCP_SERVER_PRIORITY (4.20) and ALLOWED_MCP_SERVER_PRIORITY (4.10), causing all MCP tools to be excluded by PolicyEngine.getExcludedTools().
summary.context: The tools.core setting is documented to restrict built-in core tools with an allowlist, but the wildcard DENY rule affects all tools including MCP tools. The rule needs to be scoped to core built-in tools or exclude MCP tools so that MCP trust and allow rules continue to work as intended.

steps: In packages/core/src/policy/config.ts, modify the default DENY rule emitted when settings.tools?.core is present.

Ensure the default DENY rule only applies to non-MCP / core tools (or explicitly excludes mcp_* prefix / MCP server tools) so that TRUSTED_MCP_SERVER_PRIORITY and ALLOWED_MCP_SERVER_PRIORITY rules are preserved for MCP tools.

testing_strategy.expected_behavior: When settings.tools.core is specified (e.g. []), trusted or allowed MCP tools remain allowed and are not blocked by the core tools default DENY rule.
verification_steps: Add unit tests in packages/core/src/policy/config.test.ts setting tools.core along with trusted mcpServers.
Verify that MCP tools are properly allowed and not matched or excluded by the core tools default DENY rule.
